title: How to Stop Paying International Transfer Fees (A Digital Nomad's Guide)
summary: Money without borders. Send, spend, and save across borders with Blaze, built for nomads, expats, and global businesses.
body_markdown:
Most digital nomads know they're paying fees on international transfers. What they don't know is how much.


Let's start with a number.


> **If you earn $5,000/month and pay a 3% fee on transfers, you lose $1,800 every year. That's three months of rent in Medellín.**


That 3% isn't made up. It's actually on the lower end of what most banks and transfer services charge. Some take 4–5%. PayPal can hit 5%+ when you factor in the exchange rate markup.


Here's how to stop it.


---


## 🕵️ Where the Fees Are Hiding


International transfer fees don't always look like fees. That's what makes them hard to fight.


There are three places they hide:


### 1. The Exchange Rate Markup


When your bank converts USD to MXN or COP, they use their own rate — not the market rate. The difference between the two is how they make money. A 1–2% rate markup is standard. You don't see it as a "fee." It just quietly reduces how much money arrives.


### 2. The Fixed Transfer Fee


This is the one you usually do see. Your bank charges $25–45 per wire. Western Union charges flat fees per transfer. Even Wise charges a fixed fee on top of its percentage fee.


### 3. Receiving Fees


The recipient's bank can also charge a fee to accept an international wire. In Latin America, local banks often charge $10–25 per received wire. It comes out of what you sent.


Add all three together and you're often looking at 3–5% lost per transfer.


---


## 💰 The Real Math on a $1,000 Transfer


Here's what actually happens when you send $1,000 to yourself or a contractor abroad.


Method Fee Structure What Arrives


US Bank Wire $35 flat + ~1.5% FX markup ~$950


Western Union ~$15–25 flat + 2–3% markup ~$950–$960


PayPal ~3% + FX markup ~$935–$950


Wise ~0.67% + $1.50 fixed ~$991


**Blaze** **0.5% flat** **~$995**


The difference between a bank wire and Blaze on a single $1,000 transfer: **$45.**


At $5,000/month, that's $270 a month. Every month.


---

**0.5% flat. No fixed fee. No rate markup.**


On a $1,000 transfer: $5. On a $5,000 transfer: $25. That's it.

---


## 📋 Practical Steps to Cut Your Transfer Costs


### Step 1: Figure out what you're actually paying now


Pull your last 3 months of transfers and add up what you paid. Include:


- The stated fee
- The difference between the mid-market rate and what you got


Most people are shocked when they do this math.


### Step 2: Open a Blaze account


Download the app, verify your identity, and get a US virtual account number. Takes about 5 minutes.

You'll see the 0.5% fee clearly before you confirm. Compare that number to what you paid before.


### Step 4: Update your client payment details


If you're a freelancer, share your Blaze account details with clients so payments come in directly. If you're sending to contractors, they can receive in their local currency.
